sonnet.problem: This story card has three sentences: 'First up is speaking in a tongue.' / 'Paul says that person speaks to God, not to men, and no one understands him.' / 'He utters mysteries in the Spirit.' Only the opening card may run to 3 sentences, and this is not the opening card.
sonnet.rule: **Every other story card, including the first card of a later stop, is 1 to 2 sentences.**

sonnet.problem: The true/false statement joins two claims. The first half, that a tongue speaker speaks to God and no one understands him, just repeats the story card right before it (card 3, verse 2). The second half, that the prophet speaks to people, is the only new claim and is what verse 3 supports. The statement therefore tests more than one claim and partly restates the previous card.
sonnet.rule: A true or false statement tests one claim. ... A True statement never just repeats the card before it.
